trial_court: Family Court, Ranchi, Original Suit No. 30 of 2003
case_name: Vibha Singh @ Bebi Kumari Singh vs Dilip Kumar Singh

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Vibha Singh @ Bebi Kumari Singh (wife)

facts_of_case: The wife filed a divorce suit against her husband citing cruelty and seeking a decree for dissolution of marriage. The trial court decreed the suit in 2006. The husband failed to pay maintenance as directed. The wife then filed an execution case. The husband later applied under section 25(2) & (3) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, claiming that his wife had been living an adulterous life.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse is entitled to permanent alimony if they have no source of income and are unable to maintain themselves.
legal_principles.held: The respondent has claimed that he is unemployed and has got no source of income. He is bound to maintain the Plaintiff.
use_in: divorce cases where one spouse has no income

legal_principles.principle: A court may vary, modify or rescind any order if the wife has not remained chaste or remarried.
legal_principles.held: Sub-section (2) to section 25 of the HM Act provides that the Court may vary, modify or rescind any order and, more particularly, under sub-section (3) if the Court is satisfied that the wife has not remained chaste or remarried.

outcome.final_order: The application under section 25(2) & (3) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was allowed. The husband's claim that his wife had been living an adulterous life was accepted.
